label: radeon-vllm-concurrency
platform: vLLM 0.16.1.dev0 on ROCm 7.2.1 (navi, ubuntu22.04, torch 2.9), AMD Radeon Cloud

measurement.method: N copies of the medium prompt issued in parallel; aggregate rate is total content deltas divided by wall clock for the whole batch
measurement.transport: Radeon Cloud HTTPS spaces proxy; the instance SSH port is refused from the client network and the Jupyter port returns 403, so no on-box run was possible
measurement.unit_note: chunks counts streamed SSE content deltas, not tokenizer tokens

finding: Aggregate throughput scales 7.63x across an 8x increase in load (95% efficiency) while per-request rate stays essentially flat (23.5 to 22.4 deltas/s) and median TTFT improves 3.6x (1.486s to 0.411s). Wall clock is roughly constant at ~57s whether serving 1 request or 8, which is continuous batching absorbing the load. Compare bench-results/ollama-m4air-concurrency.json, where the same step from 1 to 2 concurrent requests REDUCED aggregate throughput to 0.70x and pushed TTFT from 4.36s to 42.21s.
